Everything mathviz draws -- panel chrome, slider tracks, the legend, chart axes and gridlines, the chart palette -- is a CSS custom property with a `--vm-` prefix. To re-theme the library you redeclare tokens in your own stylesheet. There is no JavaScript configuration for colors.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
VM = window.VM
vmTheme = Generators.observe(notify => VM.plotting.onThemeChange(notify))
chartColors = VM.plotting.colors(vmTheme)
```

## Overriding tokens

A plain declaration in your own stylesheet wins, whatever order the stylesheets load in (the library's defaults are written to have zero specificity). In Quarto, list the file under `format: html: css:`.

```css
/* your styles.css */
:root {
  --vm-accent: #b45309;
  --vm-color-fn: #b45309;
  --vm-font-sans: "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif;
}
body.quarto-dark {
  --vm-accent: #fbbf24;
  --vm-color-fn: #fbbf24;
}
```

Declare dark values under one of the [dark selectors](#dark-mode) below. Tokens that don't change between themes (`--vm-radius`, `--vm-font-sans`) need declaring only once.

## The tokens

Live: each swatch is the value your browser computes for the token **right now**. Toggle the theme and watch the column change.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  vmTheme
  const rows = [
    ["Chrome", null],
    ["--vm-bg", "page background: fullscreen backdrop, the pill behind the fullscreen button, slider thumb ring, swatch tint base"],
    ["--vm-surface", "panel and controls-bar background; tooltip background (JS)"],
    ["--vm-surface-hover", "hover state of modebar and fullscreen buttons"],
    ["--vm-text", "panel text; chart font and tooltip text (JS)"],
    ["--vm-text-soft", "labels, the legend's unchecked items, play buttons; axis ticks and titles, the empty-state message (JS)"],
    ["--vm-border", "panel borders, slider tracks; axis lines, zero lines, ticks, tooltip border (JS)"],
    ["--vm-accent", "buttons, focus rings, slider fill, the active modebar button"],
    ["--vm-accent-hover", "Observable Inputs button hover"],
    ["--vm-on-accent", "text and icons drawn <em>on</em> --vm-accent: a filled button's label, the selected playback speed pill. Not white -- the dark accent is pale, and white on it measures 2.09:1. If you override --vm-accent, override this with your page background"],
    ["--vm-grid", "chart gridlines (JS only)"],
    ["--vm-radius", "panel and popover corners -- same in both themes"],
    ["--vm-radius-sm", "inputs, buttons, the legend grip -- same in both themes"],
    ["--vm-shadow", "legend, popover, modebar pill"],
    ["--vm-font-sans", "chart text and the playback popover -- same in both themes. Redeclare it if your site self-hosts a font"],
    ["Controls", null],
    ["--vm-control-h", "one height for every control a panel or controls bar holds -- text field, number readout, <code>select</code>, button -- so a row of mixed controls lines up on both edges"],
    ["--vm-label-size", "the size a control's label is set in, so it doesn't inherit the host page's body-prose size and end up taller than the value it labels"],
    ["--vm-select-chevron", "the dropdown arrow on a <code>select</code>, as a whole <code>url()</code>. It is the entire image rather than a color because var() does not resolve inside a data: URI -- which is also why each theme declares its own. Redeclare it if you change --vm-text-soft"],
    ["Chart palette (VM.plotting.colors())", null],
    ["--vm-color-fn", "the function itself, the primary trace; .vm-swatch-fn"],
    ["--vm-color-alt", "an alternate or reference trace; .vm-swatch-alt; .vm-invalid"],
    ["--vm-color-ok", "a converged or correct marker; .vm-swatch-ok"],
    ["--vm-color-muted", "de-emphasized data; .vm-swatch-muted"],
    ["--vm-color-ink", "strokes and labels that should read as text; .vm-swatch-ink"],
    ["--vm-color-warn", "a warning, a diverging iterate; .vm-swatch-warn"],
    ["--vm-color-accent2", "a third series; .vm-swatch-accent2"],
    ["--vm-color-accent3", "a fourth series; .vm-swatch-accent3"],
    ["--vm-color-halo", "the ring around a marker: white on light, the page background on dark"]
  ]
  const style = getComputedStyle(document.body)
  const table = document.createElement("table")
  table.className = "table table-sm small"
  table.innerHTML = "<thead><tr><th>Token</th><th>Current value</th><th>Used for</th></tr></thead>"
  const body = document.createElement("tbody")
  for (const [name, use] of rows) {
    const tr = document.createElement("tr")
    if (use === null) { tr.innerHTML = `<th colspan=3 style="padding-top:.8rem">${name}</th>`; body.appendChild(tr); continue }
    const value = style.getPropertyValue(name).trim()
    const isColor = /^(#|rgb)/.test(value)
    const chip = isColor ? `<span style="display:inline-block;width:1rem;height:1rem;border-radius:3px;border:1px solid var(--vm-border);background:${value};vertical-align:-3px;margin-right:.4rem"></span>` : ""
    // --vm-select-chevron resolves to a whole inline-SVG data: URI, which
    // printed in full would be the only thing on this page. Truncate, and
    // keep the real value on the title attribute.
    let shown = value
    if (shown.length > 48) shown = shown.slice(0, 45) + "…"
    const title = value.replaceAll('"', "&quot;")
    tr.innerHTML = `<td style="white-space:nowrap"><code>${name}</code></td><td style="white-space:nowrap" title="${title}">${chip}<code>${shown}</code></td><td>${use}</td>`
    body.appendChild(tr)
  }
  table.appendChild(body)
  return table
}
```

The palette is keyed by **role**, not hue. A page reads `chartColors.fn` and `chartColors.alt` rather than repeating a hex, so redefining `--vm-color-fn` recolors every primary trace on the site. `halo` deserves a word: pages used to write `line: {color: "white"}` for the ring around a marker, which is a white ring on a near-black chart in dark mode. Use `chartColors.halo`.

Only these tokens are public; a few other `--vm-*` properties the library writes at runtime are listed under [Internals](reference/internals.qmd#generated-classes) and are not for setting.

## Dark mode {#dark-mode}

The library considers the page dark when one of these matches:

```css
body.quarto-dark, html[data-bs-theme="dark"], body[data-bs-theme="dark"], html.vm-dark, body.vm-dark
```

- `body.quarto-dark` -- what Quarto's built-in light/dark toggle sets
- `[data-bs-theme="dark"]` on `html` or `body` -- Bootstrap 5.3's convention
- `.vm-dark` on `html` or `body` -- for a site with its own toggle: add the class and the library follows

If your toggle uses none of these, either add `.vm-dark` to `<html>` when it flips, or name your own selector:

```js
VM.plotting.configure({darkSelector: "html.theme-dark"})
```

and declare your dark tokens under that same selector. Match on `html` or `body`, not on an inner element (why: [Internals](reference/internals.qmd#dark-mode-detection)).

## Following the theme in a chart

Chart **chrome** -- background, axes, gridlines, tooltip -- re-themes itself on every chart when the theme flips. Nothing to do.

Chart **traces** don't, because their colors are values your page baked in. The fix is the two cells at the top of every page:

```js
vmTheme = Generators.observe(notify => VM.plotting.onThemeChange(notify))
chartColors = VM.plotting.colors(vmTheme)
```

Any cell that reads `chartColors` re-runs on a toggle. If a cell stores a color in a data structure rather than reading it at draw time, it must depend on `chartColors` too -- a bare `chartColors;` line at the top of the cell is enough.

For translucent fills use `VM.plotting.alpha("ok", 0.2)` rather than an `rgba(...)` literal: the literal stays light-mode green after a toggle while the stroke next to it lightens.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const div = document.createElement("div")
  div.style.height = "240px"
  const xs = [], ys = []
  for (let i = 0; i <= 100; i++) { const x = i / 10; xs.push(x); ys.push(Math.exp(-x / 3) * Math.sin(2 * x)) }
  Plotly.newPlot(div, [
    {x: xs, y: ys, fill: "tozeroy", fillcolor: VM.plotting.alpha("ok", 0.2), line: {color: chartColors.ok, width: 2}, name: "alpha('ok', 0.2) under an ok stroke"},
    {x: [2.4, 5.5], y: [ys[24], ys[55]], mode: "markers", marker: {color: chartColors.alt, size: 12, line: {color: chartColors.halo, width: 2.5}}, name: "halo ring"}
  ], {legend: {x: 0.55, y: 0.98}, margin: {t: 8}})
  VM.plotting.autoResize(div)
  return div
}
```

## Prose swatches

To tint a color word in running text so it matches the trace it describes: `<span class="vm-swatch vm-swatch-alt">red</span>` → <span class="vm-swatch vm-swatch-alt">red</span>. There is a modifier per palette color -- `-fn`, `-alt`, `-ok`, `-muted`, `-ink`, `-warn`, `-accent2`, `-accent3` -- plus `-accent` for the UI accent (`--vm-accent`). `vm-swatch` alone sets no color, and there is no `-halo` (it is the page background). The full table with samples is on the [Markup](markup.qmd#vm-swatch) page.

## Bringing your own stylesheet

`mathviz: {css: false}` (or simply not loading `mathviz.css`) leaves you responsible for both halves: the `--vm-*` tokens the charts read (without them the light defaults are used, in dark mode too) and the `ojs-*` / `vm-*` rules that lay out panels and position the legend. Most sites want the stylesheet plus a handful of token overrides, not a replacement.
